title: OpenAI-compat: tool selection heuristics, disambiguation hints, and robust streamed tool-message reassembly
author: Marcos Reyes
description:
Context and motivation: Users integrating OpenAI-style function/tool calling expect the model to either pick a single tool or signal that multiple candidates are possible. In practice we saw two categories of failures in production: 1) ambiguous tool_choice responses where the model returned a non-deterministic or multi-candidate selection string (e.g. "tool_choice: [search || lookup]") and 2) streamed tool messages that were fragmented across SSE chunks, causing the compat layer to either prematurely invoke a tool with partial arguments or to drop continuation fragments in the presence of transient reconnects.

This PR introduces three coordinated changes to the OpenAI compatibility layer: 1) deterministic selection heuristics with explicit disambiguation hints for downstream SDKs and clients, 2) a small schema extension to the compat mapping so tools can declare disambiguation hints and secondary scoring metadata, and 3) a robust streamed reassembly protocol that handles partial JSON payloads and provides idempotent resume semantics for interrupted streams.

High-level design summary: 
- Selection heuristics: We add an ordered precedence list to the compat layer. When the model output contains an OpenAI-style "tool_choice" entry, the compat layer will attempt to parse it in order: (a) explicit function name match, (b) tool alias match, (c) structured array of candidates (first candidate preferred), (d) textual heuristics fallback (best-effort NLP match). If parsing yields multiple plausible candidates, the compat layer emits a "disambiguation_hint" payload (see schema) instead of invoking the tool immediately. Clients that support interactive flows can surface the hint to the user or ask a follow-up question. Non-interactive clients can opt into automatic tie-breaking via a new request flag.

- Disambiguation hint schema: To preserve OpenAI compatibility while enabling richer server-side decisions, we map internal tool metadata into a minimal, backward-compatible envelope that includes: name, aliases, short_description, score_hint (float between 0-1 as string for compactness), and disambiguation_reasons (comma-separated string). This allows downstream SDKs to present contextual information rather than just a tool name. The compat layer will only include this envelope when ambiguity is detected.

- Streamed tool-message reassembly: We observed two failure modes: truncated JSON args due to SSE chunk boundaries and missed continuation fragments after a transient client disconnect. The new reassembly logic implements a safe-buffer strategy: payload fragments are appended until a well-formed JSON object is detected (verified with a tolerant parser), or until a configurable max buffer size is reached (default 64KB). On reconnect with a resume token the client provides last_seen_event_id and the server returns a resume cursor; the compat layer deduplicates re-sent fragments using sequence markers and only calls the tool after the final object is validated. We intentionally do not change the public OpenAI payload shape; the reassembly is internal to the compat layer and is opt-in behind the request flag "stream_resume_mode" for early rollout.

Backward-compat/migration notes: clients that do not understand disambiguation_hint will continue to receive the existing function/tool invocation payloads. To avoid breaking behavior, the compat layer favors conservative changes: it will only emit disambiguation_hint when ambiguity is explicit, and automatic tie-breaking defaults to the highest confidence candidate unless the request explicitly asks for a hint-first flow.

Implementation details (summary): 
- compat/openai_mapper.py: new parsing utilities to extract tool_choice variants and produce canonical internal selection intents. Includes unit-tested heuristics for alias normalization and punctuation-tolerant tokenization.
- compat/stream_reassembly.py: streaming buffer, tolerant JSON detector, resume-token state-machine, and integration tests with mocked SSE churn.
- api/handlers/tool_invocation_adapter.go: updated adapter to accept selection_intent envelope and to emit disambiguation_hint when needed. Adds metrics (tool_choice.ambiguous_count, stream_resume.attempts).
- sdk-shims/ts: small client-side opt-in flag mapping (stream_resume_mode, prefer_disambiguation_hint) and example flow in examples/openai/disambiguation-interactive.ts.

Test plan: 
- new unit tests for alias/heuristic parsing and structured-candidate precedence.
- end-to-end integration test that simulates fragmented SSE with reconnect and validates idempotent tool invocation.
- smoke test against openai-compat matrix to ensure no regressions in stable function-call flows.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add compat parsing and mapping code with tests
- [x] Add stream reassembly and resume semantics
- [x] Update adapter + metrics
- [x] Add SDK opt-in flags and example consumer flow
- [x] Update docs (compatibility note and migration guidance)

Risk and rollout: The default behavior preserves current semantics. The new disambiguation path is gated behind a request flag and a feature flag at runtime. We will enable for 10% of traffic and monitor tool_choice.ambiguous_count, tool_invocation.latency, and stream_resume.failures for 48 hours before a broader rollout.

Related linear/Jira: ENG-3248 tracks the selection heuristics work; ENG-3261 tracks the streaming resume implementation.

Example (before): the model emits: "{\"tool_choice\": \"lookup\", \"args\": \"{\\\"q\\\": \\\"redwood\\\"}\"}"

Example (ambiguous model output): "tool_choice: [lookup, search]" -> compat layer will emit disambiguation_hint: "{name: "lookup", aliases:"lookup,kv-lookup", score_hint:"0.52", disambiguation_reasons:"overlap in query terms,low-confidence"}" and will not invoke the tool until client/flow resolves.

Merge notes: Feature is behind flags and defaults to legacy behavior. See release notes for client opt-in instructions.

review_comments: Asha Gupta: Nice work. Two questions: (1) how do we surface disambiguation_hint to non-interactive SDKs? (2) should we rate-limit resume attempts to avoid DoS from noisy clients?

Marcos Reyes: Answer: non-interactive SDKs can pass prefer_disambiguation_hint=false (default) and legacy behavior applies; we added a server-side rate limiter for resume attempts (configurable per-customer), see charts/feature-flags.yaml.

Liam O'Connor: Implementation looks good. Please add a unit test for an oddball case: model emits malformed array syntax like "tool_choice: [search || lookup]" — we should normalize it to [search, lookup].
Marcos Reyes: Added test case for punctuated arrays and normalization rules in tests/unit/test_toolchoice_parsing.py
Nora Chen: Can we add an observability alert for tool_choice.ambiguous_count crossing 0.5%?
Marcos Reyes: Added metric and suggested alert in metrics/definitions.yaml; ops to review thresholds during rollout.
release_notes: Added OpenAI-compat disambiguation hints and robust streamed tool-message reassembly. Backwards compatible by default; clients can opt-in to interactive disambiguation flows and stream-resume mode. See docs/openai_compat.md for migration steps.
